'''Wolf Vielstich''' (born 18 June 1923<ref name="Krausa1999" /> in [[Munich]]; died 27 August 2021<ref name="Todesanzeige" />) was a German [[chemist]] and professor at the [[University of Bonn]] from 1965 to 1988.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Holze |first=R. |date=2013-07-01 |title=The 90th birthday of Wolf Vielstich |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10008-012-1984-0 |journal=Journal of Solid State Electrochemistry |language=en |volume=17 |issue=7 |pages=1791–1792 |doi=10.1007/s10008-012-1984-0 |issn=1433-0768}}</ref> His research focus included [[Electric battery|batteries]] and [[fuel cell]]s.<ref name="Heitbaum1974" />

== Early life ==
He worked as a graduate student with [[Heinz Gerischer]] as his thesis advisor, did a postdoc at [[Louisiana State University]] with [[Paul Delahay]] and moved to the [[University of Bonn]] in 1958. He completed his [[habilitation]] in 1965 with a book on fuel cells, after which he was appointed professor in Bonn.<ref name="Hab1965" /> In 1972 he was appointed director of the institute, he retired in 1998 from the University of Bonn.<ref name="Krausa1999" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Santos |first=Elizabeth |url=https://www.google.co.in/books/edition/Catalysis_in_Electrochemistry/rInr1JmVuUEC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Wolf+Vielstich&pg=PR9&printsec=frontcover |title=Catalysis in Electrochemistry: From Fundamental Aspects to Strategies for Fuel Cell Development |last2=Schmickler |first2=Wolfgang |date=2011-10-18 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-0-470-93473-9 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1998, he received the [[Faraday Medal (electrochemistry)|Faraday Medal]] from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].
